paper_metadata.title: Prospective study of the association between sport-related concussion and brain morphometry (3T-MRI) in collegiate athletes: A study from the NCAA-DOD CARE Consortium

quips_assessment.risk_reasoning: The study uses a large, multi-site prospective design with clearly defined inclusion/exclusion criteria and a robust matching algorithm for controls. The source population (collegiate athletes) is well-described, and the recruitment process through the CARE Consortium is standardized.

items.evidence_snippet: Contact sport athletes from football, ice hockey, lacrosse, and soccer were enrolled during the preseason.
items.reasoning: The paper specifies the types of sports and the collegiate setting clearly.

quips_assessment.risk_reasoning: The prognostic factor (concussion) is defined using a standardized consensus definition and confirmed by medical professionals. The use of matched controls further strengthens the measurement of the 'exposure'.

items.evidence_snippet: Concussion was defined per the US Department of Defense consensus as "a change in brain function following a force to the head..."
items.reasoning: A standardized clinical definition is used.

items.label: Method used for missing data
items.prompt: Appropriate methods of imputation are used for missing 'PF' data.

quips_assessment.risk_reasoning: Outcomes (brain morphometry) were measured using objective 3T MRI and processed with a validated, automated pipeline (FreeSurfer). Quality control steps (manual grading) were implemented to ensure data integrity.

items.label: Definition of the Outcome
items.prompt: A clear definition of outcome is provided, including duration of follow-up and level and extent of the outcome construct.
items.evidence_snippet: Subcortical volumes (amygdala, hippocampus, thalamus, dorsal striatum) and vertex-wise measurements of cortical thickness/volume were computed using FreeSurfer.
items.reasoning: The anatomical outcomes are precisely defined.

items.label: Valid and Reliable Measurement of Outcome
items.prompt: The method of outcome measurement used is adequately valid and reliable to limit misclassification bias (e.g., may include relevant outside sources of information on measurement properties, also characteristics, such as blind measurement and confirmation of outcome with valid and reliable test).
items.evidence_snippet: Prior work has demonstrated test-retest reliability and segmentation accuracy using the longitudinal Freesurfer pipeline
items.reasoning: The study uses a validated automated tool and cites its reliability.

items.label: Method and Setting of Outcome Measurement
items.prompt: The method and setting of outcome measurement is the same for all study participants.
items.evidence_snippet: High resolution T1-weighted images (1 mm × 1 mm × 1 mm) were acquired on 3T MRI scanners at each site.
items.reasoning: Standardized imaging protocols were used across all sites, and site was used as a covariate.

quips_assessment.risk_reasoning: The study used both a matched control design and statistical adjustment for a wide range of potential confounders, including age, sex, BMI, site, and prior concussion history.
